analyst_view.overall: Early view: Köln have gone four league games without a win, the latest a 2-1 home loss to Leverkusen, and sit only three points above the drop zone. They are also short of bodies: Timo Hübers and Ellyes Skhiri are listed out until January, Thijs Dallinga long term and Imad Rondic until late November. Leipzig have won three of their last four, including 5-2 against Augsburg, and look steadier under Martin Demichelis.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Köln's missing centre-back and midfielder should help Leipzig score, but Köln's own attack is thinned by the forward injuries, so I keep the total where the site has it.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Köln at home will push forward in spells, while Leipzig tend to attack quickly rather than camp in the opposing half. Nothing in the news moves this.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. A home side under pressure can make it scrappy, but there is no derby edge and no referee named yet. I stay with the site's figure for now.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots. Both teams should create, and Köln had to rely on goalkeeper Marvin Schwabe's saves against Leverkusen. Nothing points clearly away from the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. I lean higher because Leipzig's attack is in form (five goals against Augsburg) and Köln's defence is missing Hübers, so Leipzig should get clean looks at goal.
